title: The Non-Orientable Topology of Condorcet's Paradox
summary: Preference cycles are prevalent in problems of decision-making, and are contradictory when preferences are assumed to be transitive. This contradiction underlies Condorcet's Paradox, a pioneering result of social choice theory, wherein intuitive and seemingly desirable constraints on decision-making necessarily lead to contradictory preference cycles. Topological methods have since broadened social choice theory and elucidated existing results. However, characterisations of preference cycles in topological social choice theory are lacking.
